newsitem.title: UK: Global music sales up 4 pct in '96 - industry body.
newsitem.headline: Global music sales up 4 pct in '96 - industry body.

text.p: The overall volume of global music sales grew by four percent last year, totalling four billion units valued at $39.8 billion, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) said on Tuesday.

The industry group said compact disc sales grew by nine percent while both cassette and vinyl LP sales fell by one percent and 32 percent respectively. But the singles market experienced continued growth, with an eight percent increase in sales.
Latin America was the fastest growing region, with total sales up by almost 30 percent.

Brazil ended the year as the sixth largest music market in the world, showing an increase of sales of 33 percent. Growth in Columbia exceeded 30 percent despite prolonged economic problems, the IFPI said at a seminar held during London's Music Week.

"In 1996, around 70 percent of the world's music growth was generating in less developed markets, in particular from Latin America and Asia. This compared to only 20 percent in 1993, when global growth was at a similar level to 1996," the industry body said in a statement.
In Asia, growth of nine percent was at its highest for some years. Malaysia, Taiwan and Thailand all experienced sales growth of more than 20 percent.
Europe retained its position as the largest region for music sales, accounting for 34 percent of world sales, the IFPI said.
In Britain, sales grew by seven percent. Among medium-sized markets, Denmark and Portugal both showed growth in sales of over 15 percent.
In eastern Europe, sales grew by 14 percent overall, with CD sales increasing by almost 30 percent and cassette sales up by more than 10 percent.
However, sales grew at a slower rate in North America and Japan while Australia saw sales rise 14 percent, due in part to a larger retail base.
The IFPI figures cover music sales from 77 countries.
